title: Extract Email Domain
description:
Extract the **domain** (the part after `@`) from each customer's email, then count how many customers use each domain.

**Table: customers**

| Column | Type |
|--------|------|
| id | INT |
| name | VARCHAR |
| email | VARCHAR |
| city | VARCHAR |
| country | VARCHAR |

Output columns: `domain`, `customer_count`. Order by `customer_count` descending, then `domain`.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE customers (id INT, name VARCHAR, email VARCHAR, city VARCHAR, country VARCHAR); INSERT INTO customers VALUES (1,'Alice','alice@gmail.com','New York','USA'),(2,'Bob','bob@yahoo.com','London','UK'),(3,'Carol','carol@gmail.com','Chicago','USA'),(4,'Dan','dan@outlook.com','Mumbai','India'),(5,'Eve','eve@gmail.com','Paris','France'),(6,'Fay','fay@yahoo.com','Berlin','Germany');
solution_sql: SELECT SPLIT_PART(email, '@', 2) AS domain, COUNT(*) AS customer_count FROM customers GROUP BY domain ORDER BY customer_count DESC, domain
hints: SPLIT_PART(string, delimiter, part_number) splits a string and returns the nth part.
SPLIT_PART(email, '@', 2) returns everything after the @ sign.
explanation: `SPLIT_PART(email, '@', 2)` splits on `@` and returns the second segment — the domain. Grouping by domain and counting gives the distribution of email providers.
